title: rbac: add rollout management permissions + update default role mappings
author: Kaitlyn Nguyen
release_notes: Adds RBAC permissions used by Hosted rollout workflow (GA): create/edit/pause/rollback, plus read access for viewing rollout state and audit timeline. Updates default role templates and enterprise admin mappings accordingly.
body:
## Context
Hosted canary rollout workflow (GA) needs first-class RBAC gates for managing rollouts on Hosted routes. The control plane and Console will enforce permissions at the API boundary; this repo provides the canonical permission registry + role templates used by our authz layer.

Related:
- Linear: ENG-8429 (Entitlements/RBAC gating)
- Linear: ENG-8426 (Audit log events for rollout changes)

## What changed
### New permissions
Adds the following permissions under the `rollouts.*` namespace (names align with control-plane enforcement):
- `rollouts.read` — view rollout policy/effective routing preview, status, and history
- `rollouts.create` — create a rollout for a Hosted route
- `rollouts.update` — edit rollout configuration (weights/schedule/guardrails)
- `rollouts.pause` — pause a rollout (freeze schedule + hold weights)
- `rollouts.rollback` — rollback to baseline (force candidate to 0%, mark rollout rolled_back)

Notes:
- We intentionally keep `pause` and `rollback` separate so we can allow “operator” roles to mitigate incidents without granting full edit access.
- `rollouts.update` does NOT implicitly include `rollback`.

### Default roles updates
- `role:owner` / `role:admin` (workspace): add all rollout permissions.
- `role:developer`: add `rollouts.read` only.
- `role:operator` (oncall-ish): add `rollouts.read`, `rollouts.pause`, `rollouts.rollback`.

### Enterprise role mappings
Updates enterprise admin role mappings to include all rollout permissions (mirrors current behavior for other control-plane management actions).

## Why this design
- Separation of duties: editing schedules/guardrails is different from emergency mitigation.
- Principle of least privilege: most engineers only need read access to see effective routing + metrics.
- Compatibility with audit logging: rollback/pause are explicit, auditable actions.

## Testing
- `policy-bundle lint`
- `role template expansion` unit tests updated/added
- CI validates permission registry schema and ensures no orphan role references

## Follow-ups
- Console + control-plane will start enforcing these permissions when the GA feature flag is enabled.
- Support tooling role templates may need a dedicated “Support (read-only)” role; not included here.

## Checklist
- [x] Permissions names reviewed with control plane owners
- [x] Default roles updated with least-privilege approach
- [x] Enterprise admin mapping updated
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [x] Changelog entry
commits: rbac: update enterprise admin role mappings
tests: add role expansion coverage for rollout permissions
chore: bump policy bundle version + changelog
review_conversation:
Marcus Lin: Can we ensure `rollouts.update` does not imply rollback? Also, please confirm naming matches what control plane will check.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Yep—separate permissions. Control plane will check exact strings in this PR; synced with Ethan/Jordan on naming.

Jordan Lee: For deterministic policy evaluation, we may want to allow read access broadly. Are we comfortable giving `rollouts.read` to developer by default?
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Agree; the Console needs to show status/preview to most engineers. `read` only (no mutation) is the default for developer.

Ethan Park: Operator having rollback is good for incident mitigation, but do we need `pause` too?
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added both. Pause is safer than rollback for early triage; rollback is for confirmed bad candidate. Both are auditable and don’t allow schedule edits.

Connor O'Brien: Any rollout permission changes should include changelog entry. Also confirm version bump.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (author): Added changelog + bumped bundle version in the same PR.
